narrative.overview:
Staff spend whole event cycles in `/admin`, so it borrows the tool they already know how to read: AWS's Cloudscape design system (cloudscape.design, visual refresh), built in ERB, Tailwind and Stimulus rather than imported. The look is a cloud console's: a dark top bar, a white side navigation, breadcrumbs, a flashbar, and content laid out as bordered containers, dense tables and key-value panels. Values come from Cloudscape's published design tokens with one deliberate swap: Hack Club red replaces Cloudscape's interactive blue, deepened so every label clears AA.

The console is a translation, not a remix. Where Cloudscape has a component, the console uses its shape, spacing and states; where Attend needs one Cloudscape lacks, it is assembled from existing kit parts. Its single Hack Club gesture beyond the red is the 3px accent rail on the active side-nav link.
keyCharacteristics: Dark top navigation in both modes, white (or dark-mode slate) side navigation, bordered 16px containers
Hack Club red as the interactive colour (`--cs-accent`), Cloudscape's own status colours for state
Open Sans at 14/20, bold (700) for labels, headings and buttons
Two modes only: the app's nine themes collapse to light or dark inside the console
Status as icon + word; badges as 4px-radius chips
One content width for every page, capped at 1680px

rules.name: The Red-For-Blue Rule
rules.body: Every place Cloudscape uses its interactive blue, the console uses `--cs-accent`, and nowhere else. Red never marks an error state in the console; errors use `--cs-error`, a different red from a different ramp.

rules.name: The Two Modes Rule
rules.body: The console has Cloudscape's light and dark modes, not the app's nine themes. `admin_console_theme` maps `light` and `catppuccin-latte` to light and every other theme to dark, and the theme controller applies the same mapping client-side. New console styling is written against `--cs-*` tokens and checked in both modes, never per-theme.

rules.name: The Tailwind Remap Rule
rules.body: In light mode the console remaps Tailwind's gray, slate, blue, green, red, amber and yellow scales onto Cloudscape's ramps, so legacy utility classes land on console colours. New console markup does not rely on that remap: it uses kit classes, or a token utility such as `text-(--cs-text-muted)` when one is truly needed. Light-mode gray-400 is lifted to #71717a so legacy meta text stays AA.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, buttons, labels and tabs are sentence case ("Add staff member"). Table headers are never uppercase; the legacy adapter strips `uppercase tracking-wider` from old markup.

rules.name: The Counter Rule
rules.body: A count beside a title is a muted, regular-weight `(12)` after the title, never a badge.

rules.name: The One Page Width Rule
rules.body: Every console page shares one content area, left-aligned against the side nav and capped at 1680px. Any top-level `max-w-*` wrapper a view brings is released to that cap and stripped of its own horizontal gutter and top padding; the content area's padding is the only page gutter. A page that needs a narrower measure constrains its inner content (the wizard caps at 960px), not its outer wrapper.

rules.name: The Two-Up Counters Rule
rules.body: Key-value grids of counters (`cs-kv-3` holding counter values, and every `cs-kv-4`/`cs-kv-5`) go two-up below 768px instead of collapsing to one long column. Five-up is 3-up at tablet width and 5-up from 1024px.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: Cloudscape's 32px controls are a desktop density. Below 640px buttons, link and inline-icon buttons, inputs and selects grow to a 40px minimum, nav links, menu items, tabs and segments gain 10px vertical padding, calendar days grow, and inputs move to 16px text so iOS doesn't zoom.

rules.name: The Full-Width Action Rule
rules.body: On phones a form's actions go full width (`cs-btn-full`, and the wizard's action row stacks in reverse so the primary sits on top); from 640px they size to content, right-aligned in the wizard.

rules.name: The Visual Refresh Radii Rule
rules.body: 16 containers, 20 buttons, 12 alerts, 8 fields and menus, 4 badges. The Clipboard's 6/8/full scale does not apply inside the console.

rules.name: The Components Layer Rule
rules.body: Every `cs-*` kit component is declared inside Tailwind's `@layer components` (order pinned as `theme, base, components, utilities`), so it beats preflight and loses to utilities: `hidden`, `sm:block` and friends work on kit elements, which Stimulus controllers rely on. Only rules that must beat utilities on purpose stay unlayered: the tokens, the legacy-pattern adapter, field focus, the one page width, links in prose, and the console's dark-mode overrides (which need `:root.cs-console`'s extra specificity to beat `themes.css`).

rules.name: The Shell Boundary Rule
rules.body: The admin layout carries a tracked `<meta name="attend-shell" content="console" data-turbo-track="reload">`. Turbo swaps `<body>` but not `<html>`'s class and `data-theme`, so any visit that crosses between the console and another layout does a full page load. Don't remove the meta or add it to another layout.

rules.name: The Confirm-Don't-Colour Rule
rules.body: A destructive action on a console page is a normal button (or a link-style button), never primary and never a red fill, and it carries `turbo_confirm`. The confirmation modal is where the action becomes primary: its confirm button is the one primary in the dialog and is labelled with the action, not "OK".

rules.name: The Underlined Prose Link Rule
rules.body: Links inside running text are underlined: any non-button link inside a paragraph, alert, description, field hint, setting description or empty state is underlined automatically. A link in running text outside a paragraph (a key-value line, a table cell) takes `cs-link-inline`. Standalone links (`cs-link`), breadcrumbs, nav and link-style buttons stay un-underlined until hover. In dark mode the accent sits at 1.86:1 against body text, so colour alone cannot mark a link.

rules.name: The Admin-Only Marker Rule
rules.body: Inside the console, the project's dashed orange outline (`border-2 border-dashed border-orange-400`) marks an admin-only control or panel on a page other roles can also see. It is never used to wrap a page, or a section of a page, that only global admins can reach; there it marks nothing.

rules.name: The Button-Not-Input Rule
rules.body: Console forms submit with `f.button` / `button_tag`, never `f.submit`: `themes.css` paints `<input>` backgrounds under dark themes, which breaks the button styling.

dos: Do build console pages from the kit: page header, containers, key-value pairs, tables, `cs_status`, `cs_badge`, `cs_breadcrumbs`.
Do write console colour as `--cs-*` tokens and check both modes.
Do show state as a status indicator (icon + word); keep badges for labels and counts.
Do keep one primary button per view region.
Do put destructive actions on normal buttons with `turbo_confirm` and let the confirmation modal carry the primary.
Do underline links in running text; use `cs-link-inline` outside paragraphs.
Do let every page use the one content width; constrain inner content, not the page wrapper.
Do use sentence case for headings, buttons, labels and tabs.
donts: Don't use red for errors, or Cloudscape blue for actions; accent is interaction, status colours are state.
Don't add per-theme console styling; the console has two modes.
Don't add new Tailwind colour utilities (`bg-gray-50`, `text-blue-800`, `bg-[#…]`) to console markup; the light-mode remap is for legacy pages.
Don't declare a kit component outside `@layer components`, or it will override `hidden`.
Don't add a top-level `max-w-*` page wrapper expecting it to narrow the page.
Don't make a destructive action primary or red-filled on the page.
Don't use uppercase table headers or full-round status pills in new console markup.
Don't wrap global-admin-only pages or sections in the dashed orange admin marker.
Don't use Open Sans, `cs-*` classes or console tokens on a Clipboard surface.

narrative.overview:
Attend is the binder a good event organiser carries: tabbed, legible at arm's length, nothing on it that isn't doing a job. Every surface is a checklist in some form — an onboarding step, a consent form, a participant row, a rooming plan — and the interface's whole job is to make the state of that checklist unmistakable. Structure comes from hairline rules and tonal surfaces, not from decoration. The page is mostly quiet greys and whites; Hack Club red appears where something is actionable or wrong, and nowhere else.

The density is deliberately administrative. Body copy runs at 14px and labels at 12px because most screens carry more information than they carry prose, and the people reading them are scanning for one changed value. Type does the hierarchy work — five weights of grey across a small size range — so the layout never needs a colour to explain itself. Components are tactile where touching them matters: buttons deepen on hover, interactive cards lift and scale slightly, and the Hack Club pill button keeps its bouncy scale(1.0625) because a teenager pressing "Continue" on their onboarding should feel it respond.

The system carries eight themes on one semantic palette. Every colour resolves through a CSS custom property (--accent, --text-strong, --bg-elev), and Tailwind's own --color-* tokens are remapped inside each theme scope so ordinary utilities re-skin for free. That indirection is the system's spine: a hardcoded hex is not a shortcut, it's a theme that breaks.

Two things Attend must not look like. Not a generic Tailwind starter — undifferentiated blue-600 buttons, indigo gradients, default shadow-lg cards, the look of no decision having been made. And not a consumer event app — gradients, hero imagery, and marketing energy inside a tool people use to do a job.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders, tonal layering instead of shadows
One loud colour (Hack Club red) held to actions, alerts, and active state
Dense administrative type scale: 14px body, 12px labels, weight over size for hierarchy
Every colour semantic and themed; eight themes on one palette contract
Mobile-first single column for participants and guardians; the support desk widens into a 256px-sidebar shell on lg (the admin console has its own shell; see Admin Console)
Motion is confined to transition-colors at ~150ms, plus a small lift on genuinely interactive cards

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Hack Club red covers ≤10% of any screen. If two things on a page are red, at most one of them is a button. Its rarity is what makes a red thing mean "act on me".

rules.name: The No Literal Hex Rule
rules.body: Every colour resolves through a semantic custom property or a Tailwind token remapped in themes.css. A raw hex in a template is a theme bug: it renders correctly in light and wrong in the other seven. New work uses var(--accent), not #ec3750. The one exception is a pin drawn onto OpenStreetMap tiles: the tiles stay light under every theme, so map markers (series map, public profile map, landing map) pin their fill and white ring as literal hex; everything the app paints around the map still resolves through tokens.

rules.name: The Theme Foreground Rule
rules.body: text-white is not a colour outside the default theme. It compiles to var(--color-white), which themes.css remaps to var(--bg-elev) so bg-white re-skins — correct for surfaces, silently wrong for text. A filled surface therefore declares its own foreground in themes.css rather than trusting text-white: accent fills take --accent-on, fills that resolve to --bg-dark/--bg-darker take --text-on-dark, fills that resolve to --bg-elev-2 take --text-strong (it is a light surface under Catppuccin Latte), and unremapped literal fills pin #ffffff. Pin it with a descendant selector (.bg-x .text-white), not inheritance — a text-white on the child outranks a colour inherited from the parent.

rules.name: The Deepened Red Rule
rules.body: #ec3750 on white measures 4.02:1 — below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. WCAG's large-text exemption (3:1) starts at 18.66px bold or 24px regular, which no button in Attend reaches, so the type cannot buy its way out. The colour moves instead: wherever white text sits on red, the fill is #d42f46 (4.89:1), hovering to #b82840. #ec3750 keeps every use that carries no text on it — dots, bars, icon fills, borders, tints, and the progress bar. The two reds are one perceptual step apart; nobody sees the difference, and every white label clears AA. Themes whose own --accent already clears their --accent-on (all six Catppuccin/Dracula/Nord variants) inherit this for free; dark and solarized-dark declare --accent-fill / --accent-fill-hover because theirs do not.

rules.name: The Weight-Before-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built by moving 500 → 600 → 700 at the same size before reaching for a larger size. Attend has more levels of meaning than it has room for type sizes.

rules.name: The Fourteen Rule
rules.body: Body copy is 14px, not 16px, everywhere inside the app shell — including on red fills, which is why The Deepened Red Rule moves the colour rather than the type. The one exception is long-form prose on the docs and public-profile surfaces, which may run at 16px with a 65–75ch measure.

rules.name: The Full-Width-Then-Auto Rule
rules.body: Every primary action is w-full sm:w-auto. On a phone a button is a full-width target; on a desktop it shrinks to its content. This pattern appears on essentially every form in the app and is not optional on guardian or participant surfaces.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface is flat at rest. If you reach for a shadow, first ask whether the element actually floats. If it doesn't, it gets a border and a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: 6px for controls, 8px for containers, full for state and identity. A third value needs a reason.

dos: Do resolve every colour through a semantic custom property (var(--accent), var(--text-strong)) or a Tailwind token that themes.css remaps. There are eight themes; a literal hex serves one.

Do fill any red surface that carries white text with accent-strong (#d42f46), not accent (#ec3750). The Deepened Red Rule is an accessibility floor, not a preference, and no type size in Attend is large enough to opt out of it.
Do make every primary action w-full sm:w-auto. Guardians and participants are on phones.
Do build depth from tonal surfaces and 1px hairlines. Reach for a shadow only when the element genuinely floats.
Do pair every status colour with its word. A green pill without "Complete" in it is a colour-only signal.
Do verify new UI in a dark theme as well as light — themes.css overrides bare input, select, and textarea elements, and remaps --color-white away from white.
Do rebuild Tailwind before judging any visual change; the compiled CSS is the thing the browser sees.
Do add cursor-pointer to every button and clickable element.
donts: Don't add new bg-blue-600 buttons or ring-blue-500 focus rings. The blue running through the onboarding wizard and guardian portal (35 blue fills, 277 blue rings) is drift from a Tailwind default, not a decision. Red is the accent everywhere; converge on it when touching those files.

Don't let Hack Club red occupy area. It fills buttons, badges, and 1px borders. Large red panels, red page headers, and red backgrounds behind body copy are out — use accent-soft if a red-tinted region is genuinely needed.
Don't ship gradients, hero imagery, or marketing motion inside the app shell. Attend is a tool someone uses to do a job, not a consumer event app.

Don't introduce a webfont on a Clipboard surface. The system stack is a deliberate performance choice for guardians on slow connections and old phones. (The console's Open Sans is staff-only and loads only under /admin.)
Don't add a third container radius. 6px controls, 8px containers, full for state and identity.
Don't use rounded-full on a plain action button. A pill in Attend means state or identity; the Hack Club brand pill is the one sanctioned exception.

Don't trust text-white to be white. Outside the default theme it resolves to a surface colour; a new filled surface needs its foreground declared in themes.css per The Theme Foreground Rule, or its label disappears.
Don't suppress the focus ring. focus:outline-none is only acceptable when a focus:ring-2 replaces it in the same class list.
Don't use text-faint for anything a user has to read. It is for placeholders and disabled states only.
narrative.scope: Clipboard world: participant, guardian, onboarding, public-profile, docs and support surfaces. The /admin console is documented in extensions.console.
